newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco seeks transparency on cereals imports.
newsitem.headline: Morocco seeks transparency on cereals imports.

text.p: Morocco, which is expected to import up to 2.5 million tonnes of wheat in 1997/98, will tell local traders to keep the authorities informed about all their cereals imports in compliance with liberalisation rules.

In a circular to be released soon, the trade ministry will tell them, "Traders should from now on regularly inform the state-run Office National des Cereals et Legumineuses (ONICL) on details of their imports," a Moroccan official said on Monday.
The tightening up of this obligation is part of the authorities' measures "to push for more transparency in the cereals trade...It also aims to protect farmers and local industry," the official said.
The measure was approved by a government meeting presided over by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali last week, he added.

Earlier this year Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub said, "Morocco will face this year a serious problem to coordinate logistics of cereals imports through the country's ports, including the Casablanca harbour."
He said measures would be taken but gave no details.
The ONICL was in charge of Morocco's cereals imports until liberalisation of commodity imports was announced on May 1, 1996.
The spokesman for the Casablanca-based Nationals Cereals Committee, which groups Morocco's main private traders, was not immediately available for comment.
